choice.psg: ❶ Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. ❷ Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. ❸ Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. ❹ Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. ❺ All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. ❻ Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. ❼ Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. ❽ With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choice.ex: (A) unchanging (B) modify (C) vain 근거 ❶❷❻❼❽ 해설: (A) ❶ 시간을 일정한(불변하는) 상품으로 봄 → unchanging. elastic(탄력적인)은 ❺의 자연의 시간(more flexible time) 쪽 성질이지 인간의 시각 이 아님 / (B) ❷❻ 지구 자전 변화에 맞춰 하루에 1초를 추가함 → modify. neglect(방치하다)는 반복적으로 시간을 덧붙이는 행동과 반대 / (C) ❼ the false hope + ❽ It doesn’t. → vain. justified(정당한)는 필자의 평가와 정반대. 요약문 해석: 인간은 시간을 (A) 변하지 않는 것으로 여기게 되었지만, 변화하는 바람과 달의 중력 같은 자연의 힘은 지구의 자전을 계속 바꾸어 놓는다. 이 에 대응하여 우리는 자연이 우리의 체계에 굴복할 것이라는 (C) 헛된 희망에 매달리며 시간 측정 방식을 반복적으로 (B) 수정한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge this mistake. ❷ On twenty-six occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone’s day to adjust for the Earth wobbling and the rate of its spin changing. ❸ For instance, when El Niño, a climatic system in the Pacific, causes wind speed to change dramatically, it can slow the rotation of the Earth slightly. ❹ Indeed, the Earth’s spin is generally slowing because the moon’s gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting longer by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. ❺ Such events disturb the similarity between man-made time and more flexible time based on the Earth’s naturally occurring rotation. ❻ When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. ❼ We try to force our fixed, man-made view of time on to nature in the false hope that it will yield. ❽ It doesn’t.
choice.body: Humans have come to regard time as (A)________, but natural forces such as shifting winds and the moon’s gravity keep altering the Earth’s spin. In response, we repeatedly (B)________ our timekeeping, clinging to the (C)________ hope that nature will bend to our system.

choice.ex: (A) irregular (B) discrepancy (C) correct 근거 ❷❸❹❺❻ 해설: (A) ❷ 지구의 흔들림·자전 속도 변화, ❸ 엘니뇨로 자전이 느려짐, ❹ 달의 중력으로 점점 느려짐 → irregular. uniform(일정한)은 반대 / (B) ❺ 인간 이 만든 시간과 자연의 시간 사이의 유사성이 깨짐 → discrepancy. harmony(조화)는 반대 / (C) ❷❻ 그 차이에 맞추려고 1초를 추가함 → correct. ignore(무시하다)는 초를 추가하는 행동과 모순, widen(넓히다)은 초를 추가하는 목적(❷ 맞추기 위해)과 반대. 요약문 해석: 엘니뇨와 달의 끌어당김 같은 자연적 요인은 지구의 자전을 (A) 불규칙하게 만들어, 시계의 시간과 행성의 실제 움직임 사이에 (B) 불일치를 만들어 낸다. 당국자들은 우리의 하루에 여분의 초를 조용히 끼워 넣음으로써 그것을 (C) 바로잡는데, 필자는 이를 시간에 대한 잘못된 관점에 뿌리를 둔 관행으로 본다.
choice.psg: ❶ Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge this mistake. ❷ On twenty-six occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone’s day to adjust for the Earth wobbling and the rate of its spin changing. ❸ For instance, when El Niño, a climatic system in the Pacific, causes wind speed to change dramatically, it can slow the rotation of the Earth slightly. ❹ Indeed, the Earth’s spin is generally slowing because the moon’s gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting longer by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. ❺ Such events disturb the similarity between man-made time and more flexible time based on the Earth’s naturally occurring rotation. ❻ When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. ❼ We try to force our fixed, man-made view of time on to nature in the false hope that it will yield. ❽ It doesn’t.
choice.body: Natural factors such as El Niño and the moon’s pull make the Earth’s rotation (A)________, creating a (B)________ between clock time and the planet’s real motion. Officials (C)________ it by quietly inserting extra seconds into our days, a practice the writer sees as rooted in a mistaken view of time.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: The writer suggests that the practice of adding seconds was first proposed by scientists studying El Niño.

choice.ex: 원문은 1초 추가 관행의 기원이나 누가 처음 제안했는지 전혀 언급하지 않음(원문 밖 기원). 엘니뇨는 ❸에서 자전을 느리게 하는 예시 로만 나옴. 나머지는 ❷❺(자전 변화에 맞추려 1초 추가 = 보조 맞추기) / ❸(풍속 변화 → 자전이 약간 느려짐) / ❻(without your knowledge) / ❼❽(false hope, It doesn’t.)에서 추론 가능. ① 근거 없음(정답) — 필자는 초를 추가하는 관행이 엘니뇨를 연구하던 과학자들에 의해 처음 제안되었다고 시사한다. ② 근거 ❸ — 태평양 풍속의 변화는 지구가 얼마나 빨리 도는지에 약간의 영향을 미칠 수 있다. ③ 근거 ❻ — 대부분의 사람들은 자신의 하루에 약간의 시간이 더해졌다는 것을 모른 채 하루를 보낸다. ④ 근거 ❷❺ — 필자는 여분의 초가 시계의 시간을 지구의 실제 자전과 보조를 맞추기 위해 끼워 넣어진다는 것을 암시한다. ⑤ 근거 ❼❽ — 경직된 시간 개념을 자연에 강요하려는 우리의 시도는 결국 실패하게 된다.
choice.psg: ❶ Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge this mistake. ❷ On twenty-six occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone’s day to adjust for the Earth wobbling and the rate of its spin changing. ❸ For instance, when El Niño, a climatic system in the Pacific, causes wind speed to change dramatically, it can slow the rotation of the Earth slightly. ❹ Indeed, the Earth’s spin is generally slowing because the moon’s gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting longer by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. ❺ Such events disturb the similarity between man-made time and more flexible time based on the Earth’s naturally occurring rotation. ❻ When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. ❼ We try to force our fixed, man-made view of time on to nature in the false hope that it will yield. ❽ It doesn’t.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: wishing that people would finally accept nature’s flexible time in place of their clocks
mistakenly expecting that the natural world will eventually conform to the rigid time we have created
expecting that the extra seconds will make our days longer and more productive
hoping that nature will produce more crops if we manage our time more efficiently
fearing that natural forces will someday destroy our system of measuring time
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 우리는 자연이 굴복할 것이라는 헛된 희망을 지니고 우리의 고정된, 인간이 만든 시간에 대한 관점을 자연에 강요하려고 노 력한다. 해설: it = nature, yield = (강요에) 굴복하다·따르다. 고정된 인간의 시간관을 자연에 강요하며 자연이 그것에 맞춰 줄 것이라 기대하지만 'false' hope이 고 ❽ It doesn’t.로 실패가 확인됨. ②는 yield의 문자적 의미(작물을 산출하다)를 이용한 함정, ③은 굴복하는 주체를 인간으로 뒤집음(자연이 아니라 사 람이 받아들임), ④는 원문에 없는 과장된 두려움, ⑤는 '하루가 생산적이 됨'이라는 무관한 내용으로 밑줄의 대상(자연)과 맞지 않음. ① 사람들이 마침내 시계 대신 자연의 유연한 시간을 받아들이기를 바라며 ② 자연 세계가 결국 우리가 만든 경직된 시간에 순응할 것이라고 잘못 기대하며 ③ 여분의 초가 우리의 하루를 더 길고 생산적으로 만들 것이라고 기대하며 ④ 우리가 시간을 더 효율적으로 관리하면 자연이 더 많은 작물을 생산할 것이라고 바라며 ⑤ 자연의 힘이 언젠가 우리의 시간 측정 체계를 파괴할까 두려워하며
choice.body: When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. We try to force our fixed, man-made view of time on to nature in the false hope that it will yield. It doesn’t.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) independent — (B) stiffen — (C) trivial
(A) cooperative — (B) release — (C) essential
(A) cooperative — (B) stiffen — (C) essential
(A) independent — (B) release — (C) essential
(A) cooperative — (B) release — (C) trivial
choice.ex: (A) cooperative (B) release (C) essential 근거 ❶❺❻❼❽ 해설: (A) ❶ opposing muscles ~ shorten and lengthen + ❺ a system of coordination = 협력하는 쌍 / (B) ❷❹ 한쪽이 수축하면 다른 쪽은 relax = 풀어 주다 / (C) ❼ Movement depends on what muscles don’t do, as much as ~ + ❽ Both are necessary = 필수적인. independent(독립적 인)는 ❺ 조정 체계와 반대, stiffen(경직되다)은 ❷❹ relax와 반대, trivial(사소한)은 ❽ Both are necessary와 반대. 요약문 해석: 팔다리의 모든 움직임은 (A) 협력하는 쌍으로 작동하는 근육에 의존한다. 한쪽이 수축하면 다른 쪽은 (B) 풀어 주어야 한다. 이런 의미에서 신체 활동은 역설적인데, 근육이 하지 않고 삼가는 일이 근육이 적극적으로 하는 일만큼 (C) 필수적이기 때문이다.
choice.psg: ❶ When your hand is hanging at your side and then you lift it, opposing muscles on your upper arm shorten and lengthen ― contract and relax ― to bend the elbow. ❷ Biceps contract, and triceps relax. ❸ Reversing the motion, when you drop your hand back down, muscles reverse roles. ❹ Triceps contract, and biceps relax. ❺ Lift your hand or drop it, and muscle shows what it is: a system of coordination, managed by orchestrated tension. ❻ As arms and legs rotate around joints, muscles activate and deactivate, contract and relax. ❼ All physical activity is paradoxical, in this sense: Movement depends on what muscles don’t do, as much as it depends on what they do. ❽ Both are necessary, each in its time ― and the same is true of each side of the pairs of concepts shaping how we talk of muscles. ❾ Start with nature versus nurture: Some people are stronger or more muscular than others; is the difference inborn, or does it depend on what people do? ❿ To the latter question: What do you do? ⓫ Do you have to lift weights, or is walking enough exercise? ⓬ How should you do the exercise? ⓭ Should you move fast or slowly? ⓮ Lift heavy weights or lighter ones? ⓯ Put like that, basic questions about muscle may sound like they have one right answer. ⓰ Oppositions can polarize. ⓱ But where muscle is concerned, few oppositions are true polarities. ⓲ Look closely, and most prove to be paradoxes. ⓳ Born and made, heavy and light, fast and slow: Those opposites actually complete each other.
choice.body: Every movement of a limb relies on muscles that work as (A)________ pairs: when one side contracts, the other side must (B)________. In this sense, physical activity is paradoxical, since what muscles refrain from doing is as (C)________ as what they actively do.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

(A) inherited — (B) harmony — (C) incompatible
